content:
maria_support: Raised an escalation for AcmeApps — they say streaming responses abruptly terminate with a client-side 'Broken pipe' and our dashboard shows a 5xx/billed event. request_id=req_0a1b2c. Can runtime/SRE confirm classification and whether this should be billed?
escalation-bot: incident created: #inc-2799988888 — priority P2 (customer billing impact)
tom_eng_runtime: Looking. Do we have full request/headers and the client stack? Is this using chunked transfer/HTTP1.1 or HTTP/2?
maria_support: They run Node fetch behind Cloudflare, chunked transfer. Trimmed gateway logs below:
```
2026-03-15T12:02:05Z REQ=req_0a1b2c stream: chunked body start
2026-03-15T12:02:07Z REQ=req_0a1b2c gateway: write to socket failed: broken pipe (EPIPE)
2026-03-15T12:02:07Z REQ=req_0a1b2c gateway: classified 5xx -> 502
```
lee_sre: That pattern usually means the client closed the connection mid-stream. Our current heuristic marks early EOF / write failures as 502 and increments classified_5xx, which then feeds billing.
hana_support: Customer reports they were billed for ~200 tokens while they claim only headers were sent. They want a refund if this was a client disconnect.
tom_eng_runtime: We recently tightened the EOF heuristic to detect partial writes. Need to check whether EPIPE vs ECONNRESET paths are being treated incorrectly. @lee_sre can you pull tcpdump around req_0a1b2c?
lee_sre: On it — starting capture for that request id and a quick local repro. Quick curl repro I'll run: `curl -N --http1.1 -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" http://gateway/stream` and abruptly close client.
devon_billing: FYI billing: logic currently uses `classified_5xx` to decide refunds programmatically; manual review needed if classification flips. We can do manual credit for confirmed misbills.
tom_eng_runtime: Found a gateway bug: when proxy write() returns EPIPE on a half-closed socket we treat it as gateway_error and return 502 while still marking tokens as served. We should map EPIPE + no-followup-data -> client_abort and not count as 5xx. I'll prepare a patch to change classification and emit a new tag `reason:socket_halfclose`. Also adding extra sanity: check if remote FIN seen in tcp trace before counting.
maria_support: Customer wants immediate mitigation. Can we suppress billing for req_0a1b2c and any with the same pattern in last 24h?
devon_billing: Yes — once SRE outputs a list of affected request_ids, we can queue manual credits for AcmeApps and mark them as refunded in billing.
tom_eng_runtime: Patch built and running to canary (gateway-canary-3). Change summary: treat EPIPE/no-body-as-client-abort; increment `client_disconnects` metric; decrement `classified_5xx` for these cases; emit `reason:socket_halfclose`. Rolling for 15m and monitoring 5xx/ClientDisconnect ratios.
lee_sre: Confirmed tcpdump shows FIN from client just before EPIPE for req_0a1b2c — classification should flip after canary. Will gather matching req ids from last 24h and post.
maria_support: Great — I'll tell AcmeApps we have a patch rolling, will provisionally credit until SRE gives final list. Thanks all :thumbsup:
